title: Answering Questions
subtitle: Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha
description: Answering Questions — a themed treasury of teachings gathered by the Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha.

articles.title: What is the Relevance of Sixth Verse of Upadeshamrit?
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Srila Gurudev elaborately explains the sixth verse of Upadeshamrit. He advises not to incur offense to any Vaishnava by observing his external behavior or bodily defects. If we do so then we will be deprived of his grace. In relation to this, Srila Gurudev also explained a verse from Srimad Bhagavad Gita, ‘api cet su-durācāro…’ He concludes his answer by emphasizing the utmost necessity of surrender to Guru, Vaishnava and Bhagavan without which there cannot be any devotion.

blocks.text: Question: This question is from Mahesvar Das, London. In the sixth verse of Upadeshamrita written by Srila Rupa Goswami, he explains that we should not see the pure Vaishnava with our material vision. This I can understand up to a certain extent. But going through the verse 9.30 of Srimad Bhagavad Gita, I relate it with some confusion. My question is, at what level of sadhana does verse six of Upadeshamrita become relevant?

Answer:
You know the sixth verse of Upadeshamrita,

“Devotees in this world should not be seen from a material perspective. Any imperfections found in their natures or their appearance should be overlooked for such faults are like the foam and mud in the water of the Ganges. Such things appear due to the nature of water, but the divine nature of the Ganges is never diminished.”

Here Rupa Goswami who is the original guru of our preceptorial channel, and our guruvargas are his followers, has written Upadeshamrita. He is the grace incarnate form of Krishna, he has given a warning. Although seeing or observing defects in the nature or body due to some disease etc. of a devotee, you should not think them as worldly people. Worldly people have got material bodies and material egos and they are devoting their whole energy for the material benefits. Devotee, devotion and Supreme Lord, these three are eternal. All the Vaishnava acharyas had substantiated that. If they are not eternal then that is not shuddha-bhakti, pure devotion. The lotus feet of Supreme Lord are eternal. Devotees who are serving His lotus feet are also eternal, then devotion can be eternal. By the grace of Supreme Lord they are serving Him. You are daily meditating the verse from Rig-veda during your morning and evening sandhya,

lines: sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ divīva cakṣur ātatam
tad viprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ sam indhate

blocks.text: The lotus feet of Supreme Lord are transcendental, ‘sat’. ‘Hari om tat sat’. Hari is transcendental and His lotus feet are also transcendental, beyond the compression of human material sense organs, mind and intellect, that is called ‘tat’. This body is non-eternal, and so sense organs are also non-eternal. When the body will perish, sense organs will also perish, even during our life time also we may lose our sense organs. So by this non-eternal body and non-eternal sense organs how we can have contact with eternal, transcendental thing. It is irrational, never possible. Diviva chakshur-atatam. Diviva means self-effulgent. You should remember the translation of the verse of Gita by our most revered siksha-guru, Param Pujyapad Swami Maharaj. You have to remember always, we should not think, it has become stale. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu heard the whole biographies of Dhruva and Prahlad from Gadadhar Pandit for hundreds of times, after hearing He would say, “I want to hear again.” Because Supreme Lord is transcendental, His associates are transcendental, His glories are also transcendental and infinite. We may say, “I have already heard, you speak something new to me,” but Chaitanya Mahaprabhu wanted to hear from Gadadhar Pandit again and again to teach the novice votaries, those who want to get spiritual realization, you should go through the biographies of the pure devotees repeatedly. Our Saraswati Goswami Thakur wrote one hymn in Bengali, He mentioned in that,

lines: śikṣā dila yāhā, cinta sei saba

blocks.text: Sambandh-gyan. He did not give any reference from any other scripture, he gave it from Chaitanya Charitamrita. What Chaitanya Mahaprabhu taught to Sanatan Goswami, you remember that. It is the basis. You have already heard it but you have not heard it because you are not established in it. If you hear something but if you are doing just the opposite of what you have heard then it is not called hearing. Foundation should be strong otherwise if you construct a building, it will fall down. You are preaching at different places I know, you have heard it I know. And you are speaking about this I know, yet I would say you are not well established in this knowledge, by your behaviour. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu taught to Sanatan Goswami about Sambandh-gyan: who am I and what my relation with Supreme Lord is. Every time we hear and forget. Supreme Lord is infinite. The words expressing Him are also infinite. They cannot be stale. They can never be stale. If you hear for infinite time, again you want to hear the same. But if you say, “I have already heard, I have no necessity to hear it again”, then you have heard nothing. When actual hearing will be there, then you will desire to hear that again and again. Harinam Mahamantra is one but every step you may have the fresh taste of Hare Krishna, Radha-Krishna mantra. It will never become stale. Here Rupa Goswami have given a warning. By seeing outside behaviour and habits of some Vaishnavas, if you speak anything ill of them then you commit an offence to them. It will be an obstacle to your spiritual realization. There may be some defect in them. What sort of defect? In their nature, there may be peevishness, i.e. some devotees are irritating in nature. By seeing that you should not behave roughly with them. There may be lethargy (in some devotee), but they have dedicated themselves fully for the service of Sri Krishna. There may be some sort of bodily constitutional defects due to some disease etc., his complexion may not be good. He may not be so beautiful, you should not see that. If you see it and behave with them roughly then Supreme Lord will be dissatisfied. Although they have got this sort of irritating nature, they have accepted the sadguru, they are performing bhajan. That you have to see. Inside they are simple hearted. We should very carefully think, outside you may be very polite, you may behave very nicely and you may use very sweet words but inside there is hypocrisy, which you are finding in the whole world now. Such persons are very dangerous and they may harm you. I have heard many incidences in India also. They deceive others by showing kind behaviour, courtesy etc., their motives are not right. But sadhu’s motives are.. They are simple hearted from inside. Outside he may use some harsh or irritating words, but that is not so dreadful to you, he will not harm anybody because he is simple hearted. That is actual necessity of a sadhu. If simple heartedness is absent and outside polite behaviour is there with some evil motive, externally he looks like a sadhu but he is asadhu. I heard, such cases came to me. I warn someone to not trust that kind of person but he said, “No, he is very good,” ultimately he was totally deceived. Those are dangerous persons. God is residing in the heart of devotees, so by seeing some external defects you should not decide to speak to them some sort of ill words. You will commit offence to their lotus feet, by disregarding them or ignoring them. If you do like that then you will be loser, he will not be the loser. So this warning is given by Srila Rupa Goswami. Without simple heartedness, no devotee can perform bhajan. Wherever simple heartedness is absent, bhajan is absent. That is essential, it must be there. We should not see the pure Vaishanava with our material vision. He (Mahesvara Das) is writing, he understands this up to certain extent.

Astavakra Muni was a powerful sadhu. But his body was bending from eight sides and people used to laugh seeing him walking. But he was a great saint. Somebody has said there, “A great saint has come to you and you are laughing by seeing his body, you are committing a great offence. You will be a loser, he will not be a loser. You will be deprived of his grace.”
Here he is saying, he can understand this verse up to certain extent, but again there is another verse in Gita. How to reconcile with Gita? Krishna also has warned us.

“Even if one commits the most abominable action, if he is engaged in devotional service he is to be considered saintly because he is properly situated in his determination. He quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly that My devotee never perishes.”

”He was worshiping Me and now he has given up? No, he is still worshiping Me, he is worshiping Me with sincerity.” But due to his previous births, after 80 lakhs of births we have got this human birth and in human birth we did so many bad deeds. Those impressions were there. Due to those impressions, he might have done one wrong thing, very wrong thing; illicit connection with women we may say, but don't disregard him because he will have repentance to the extreme, “I did a great wrong thing,” he will say and he will cry. He will pray for the grace to Guru Vaishnava. You wait for some time, he will become sadhu. He will get absolute bliss and transcendental realm, there it is written. “You should not behave with him harshly then I (Krishna) shall be displeased.” He is trying, he is trying his best. But there are waves of bad thoughts and good thoughts. And sometimes bad thoughts also come, and by bad thoughts he might have done some wrong, because of the influence of that. Do not take decision and ignore him, then you will be loser, “I (Krishna) shall be displeased.” If God is displeased then you will not get the actual benefit. God is seeing that the person is trying, trying, trying, but due to previous bad impressions he might have done something wrong, api cet su-durācāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk, but he did not give up his bhajan, he is doing bhajan, worshiping, ananya-bhāk with one-pointed devotion (not worshipping any demi-god) or he has not taken another way of worship—yoga-patha, karma-patha, jnana-patha. No, no, he is not doing that. He is doing suddha-bhakti (unalloyed devotion), he is trying to please, yet there may be some mishap. Don't disrespect him. “If you disrespect him, saying something against him then I shall be displeased. Your objective is to please Me.” With that one warning He ordered Arjuna, go to the karmis, to the jnanis, to the yogis and to the worshipers of demi-gods and declare, taking the oath that My, Krishna's devotee, will not be ruined, will never be ruined. Declare it everywhere.

The life of suddha-bhakta is one-pointed devotion to Supreme Lord. That he is sticking to and trying to do. So that life (sadhan) is there, he has not given up. Those who are deceitful they do all these criminal works and they have got no repentance. They are deceitful, hypocrites, they will go to hell. But there may be some devotees very sincere, but unable to check themselves sometimes maybe. “Don't speak ill of them, then I (Krishna) shall be dissatisfied. He is on the right path. He is the part of My potency and he has accepted that and with that relation he is trying to serve Me. He has not given up.” Krishna told in that verse to Arjuna that you declare everywhere that My devotees will never be ruined, nobody can do anything to them. So much affection Krishna has got for His devotees, those who try to serve Him sincerely.
Now here, he is asking, “How I should reconcile?” See, you should not disregard any sadhu who has got some bodily defects or defects in his nature.

This shows the weakness of Supreme Lord towards the devotees who are trying to worship Him. It is a kind of encouragement to us. While we want to worship sometimes evil thoughts come and we become disappointed that we cannot worship. But Krishna has given this assurance that if you are sincere you will be rescued: “I am at your back. You do not give up steadfastness towards Me.”

He (Mahesvar Das) is saying that he has confusion on this verse. His question is, “At what level of sadhan this shloka of updesamrit becomes relevent?” You see!! At the level of sadhana, how will you understand? It is very difficult. Because we have got the material ego. Therefore in the sadhan-bhakti, arrangement has been given. Our Gurudev and Guruvarga asked us to worship deities. We have no sharanagati. We speak about sharanagati but we do not have sharanagati. Without sharanagati there cannot be any devotion. So you should worship deities, you should engage yourself in the service of guru, give your sense organs and object of sense organs for the service of guru and ultimately, yourself completely. It ends with sharanagati to guru. It also ends in the worship and sharanagati to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and sharanagati in Radha-Krishna. Then after that you can perform bhakti, before that you cannot perform bhakti. That sharanagati is not so easy, because we have got the mundane relations in the house. We have also got mundane ego and worldly desire are also there. We have to give our energy for them. So we have got connection with them and so it is difficult to think that we are of Krishna. But perform deity worship by uttering the mantra. When a pure devotee gives something to Supreme Lord, there is no requirement of ritualistic performance. Supreme Lord will accept it directly. But generally we do not belong to that group, so we have to take the help of mantra and for that we are to take initiation. After taking initiation, when you offer something to Supreme Lord, Guru, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Radha-Krishna with uttering the mantras, then although I have got no such pure devotion, the mantra is coming in the preceptorial channel through Supreme Lord. So when you utter that mantra and offer then there is the possibility of His acceptance. You drive importance to the preceptorial channel. I have seen myself during Braja Mandal Parikrama at the time when Guru Maharaj was present. That time we used to do Braja Mandal Parikrama on foot. We had been to Nanda-ghat. It is a secluded place. We stayed in the camps. That time one person was bitten by a dog. All advised him to go to Mathura and take injections, otherwise it is dangerous. Two persons had been engaged to take him to Mathura. They were very much disheartened because if they go then there will be a break in their circumambulation of Braja Mandal. It requires two, three days or even more. It may require two, three, four, five days. Nobody can say how many days. They heard from somebody that Srauti Maharaj, elder God brother of our Guru Maharaj, was there, he had the knowledge of removing the poison of dragon bite by mantra. Then all came to him and I was also there and requested him, “If you can do this then they are not to go from here. They will have the opportunity to circumambulate the whole Braja Mandal. Otherwise they will be disappointed.”

He said, “No, I used to do this when I was in house. I was with another Guru, their preceptorial channel was different. Now you worship Krishna; why do you want to engage me in this? No I shall not do it.”

But they are pressing him and because of their pressure he agreed to do so. He asked them to bring an earthen pot, a log and other required things. As per his direction they brought everything. After bringing that, that person was asked to sit over the log, he sat on the timber and he stood up and he was also to bring sand from the Jamuna River and other things. And as he uttered mantra, he was moving and that man was also moving. No machine was there, but they both were moving. We were astonished to see. What is this? No, there is no machine, nothing. How they are moving? About one hour or more he did it and said that all poison is removed and you can take him. They all were glad and they surrounded Srauti Maharaj, “Please teach us, please teach us.” “No, No, you will not get it. You have to accept that preceptorial channel. You have to go there and worship and take mantra from them.” That person realized and I was previously realized under him, for that reason this is effective. Even if I teach you, you will not be able to learn it. You have to perform penance. Why you should do this for this mundane benefit? Worship Krishna, you have got the preceptorial channel. You will get the ultimate goal, everything. You should not spoil your time for the question (from Mahesvar Das), at what level of sadhana does the verse is relevant? Sadhana-bhakti, when they are doing sadhan-bhakti they have to start from Upadeshamrita and Sikshastaka. Upadeshamrita will help us to understand Sikshastaka written by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

First it is started from this shloka. You have to control your tongue. You should not speak anything prohibited against Krishna, Vaishnava or anybody. You should not behave like that. You have to control your mind and you should have no other desire. If there is desire and if there is an obstacle in fulfilling that desire then you will be furious, Krodha will come. So the basis is there, in the first verse. Then gradually we will go upwards. It will take time. We have to have patience and you have to go through Upadeshamrita and Sikshastaka in Braja Mandal Parikrama. In relation to this verse also, the conditioned souls often offensive thoughts will manifest due to anartha within our minds. By thinking these bad thoughts, is this still to be considered Vaishnava aparadh? Because for a novice, neophyte, this first stage is a kind of fight with evil thoughts, you have to struggle. When evil thoughts come you have to suppress them. Krishna has advised in the Gita. When Arjuna said to Krishna,
It is very difficult to control the mind. It is so restless, more restless than wind, air. What Krishna is saying there?

I agree with you, it is very difficult, but you are māha-bāho (mighty-armed one). Every living being, if he is sincere, Supreme Lord will come at his back. He will give power, His Grace Incarnate form will come. Impossible can be possible. He is equal to all. Those who surrender to Him, He also comes to help them and He will send His Grace Incarnate form. There is no fear about this. But you should be sincere. But at the time when evil thoughts come, you should try to suppress it, it is possible that again you may do some wrong things. But this time the evil thoughts will come with less momentum. If you try to suppress it, momentum will be less and gradually it will be removed. And good thoughts will come, you have to encourage them, at that time you have to worship as much as you can. When you have tendency to perform Bhajan, you do it because it will not remain for all the time. Again evil thoughts will come. If you do it, then when evil thoughts will envelope you, at that time you will not be able to do Bhajan like the previous time. But next time when that force of desire to serve will come again, it will come with double force. In this way ultimately evil thoughts will be suppressed and good thoughts will prevail. In this way gradually it will be done.

articles.title: Who Can Speak Harikatha?
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Srila Gurudev explains that only a realized soul with realized transcendental spiritual form can sing the glories of Supreme Lord. It is not possible to speak about the transcendental subjects for enslaved jivas. If someone has the vanity that he can speak about Supreme Lord then it would be just delivering a speech.

blocks.text: Question: Who can speak Harikatha?
Answer:

lines: siddha-deha diyā, vṛndāvana-mājhe, sevāmṛta karô̍’ dāna,
piyāiyā prema, matta kôr̍i’ more, śunô nija-guṇa-gāna

blocks.text: “Giving me a spiritual body within the transcendental realm of Vrindavan, bestow upon me the nectar of Your service. Thus I will become madly intoxicated with pure love by drinking the nectar of such service. Just hear about Your own glories.”

We shall have to think very carefully about this. Here Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur has prayed, “O Lord! Please give me a realized transcendental form, in the transcendental realm Vrindavan.” Supreme Lord is transcendental. The word ‘transcendental’ I have explained as per dictionary but there is some difficulty. In material language it very difficult to express the ancient Indian spiritual words. The meaning of the word ‘transcendental’ is beyond the comprehension of human beings, beyond the mind, intelligence, sense organs etc. It will descend to a completely surrendered soul. So, he is praying to Supreme Lord Krishna or Radha-Krishna, “Please give me a realized form, siddha-deha. You are in the transcendental realm and nirgun (beyond the three modes of material nature) and I am in this mundane world with this material body. How can I come in contact with You and speak about You? Please bestow me realized transcendental spiritual form. And also bestow upon me the ambrosia.” The actual ambrosia is the service of Sri Krishna, not the nectar that emerges from the milk ocean. That is worldly nectar but transcendental nectar or ambrosia is service of Sri Krishna. Krishna Himself can give this. So here he is praying, “Please give me that service and make me drink the divine love-prem.” Without prem, you cannot have the realization of Supreme Lord, who is all- existence, all-knowledge and all- bliss, Who is transcendental, beyond this mundane realm completely, by your own capability you cannot know Him. Whatever endeavour you do, everything will be failure.

You make me drink Your prema and You speak through my mouth Your glories and You hear, that is Harikatha. How can I speak? I have got misconception of self, ‘I am this material body’ and material desires. Where there are material desires, material body and material vanity, with that kind of material ego, you cannot have any kind of entrance in that transcendental, spiritual realm. That is the difficulty. Why do we spend so much time to pray the grace of Guru and Gauranga and uttering hymns (before starting speaking)? There is some necessity for that. If I have got the vanity that I can speak, then that is just delivering speech, it will have no contact with Supreme Lord.

articles.title: Who Am I and Why Three Kinds of Suffering Disturb Me?
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Srila Gurudev explains the root cause of suffering for enslaved jivas as the desire of dharma, artha, kama and moksha. When they will be uprooted, one will get Divine love.

blocks.text: Question: I humbly beg for Your grace to me, please accept me as Your servant. Please explain to me who I am and why three kinds of suffering disturb me. By Your causeless mercy alone will I be able to understand the answer to these very important questions. Srila Gurudeva, I turn to You in my prayers many times, but now I want to dedicate ‘my’ life to Your service totally, and I want ‘my’ son to develop devotion for Krishna, in this I see the sense of life for the nearest period. Teach me how to develop Sharanagati. There is no way I can understand it without Your mercy! How can I, the householder, live to please You and Gauranga?

Answer: Sufferings are of four types—dharma (religion), artha (economic development), kama (sense gratification), moksha (liberation). We actually desire those. If we get distress as a result, we call that as suffering. Sri Narada has instructed Sri Vyasdev at Sri Badrikashram. “People of this world desire dharma, artha, kama, moksha. They perform dharma for mundane benefits, they desire money, sense gratification and also liberation”, Sri Vyasdev said “I have made provision for those things. But I am not satisfied. That is why I came here to this place.”
Sri Vyasdev knows everything but he inquired for our benefit. He is not a conditioned person. He asked his Gurudev and his Gurudev answered.

Sri Vyasdev said, “If we perform some good deeds, we get some or other benefit. People also want money, sense gratification and liberation. Even after I provided all these things for their benefit, I am not at peace.”
Sri Narada Risi said, “You have done a very bad thing. People are already inclined towards perishable benefits. That is the reason for suffering and you have encouraged them.”
“I have given them a path for liberation also.”
“You have done an even worse thing. You have destroyed their bhakti.”
“What should I do?”
“When you meditate on the scriptures that describe beyond these four things—dharma, artha, kama, moksha—your root cause for suffering will be uprooted. Then you will get prema.”

This is written in Srimad Bhagavat. There are four main verses (Srimad Bhagavatam Canto 2 Chapter 9, verses 33 to 36) and it is elaborated in the entire Bhagavat Puran. There are also teachings of renunciation and knowledge in that scripture. If we read that scripture we will get peace.

articles.title: Instructions to Devotees Entering Household Life
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Srila Gurudev was asked to give instructions to a devotee entering married life. Srila Gurudev advised him to live Krishna-centered life with the sole aim of serving Krishna only.

blocks.text: A household devotee should make Krishna as the centre of his life (do Krishna Samsara) and should serve Krishna.

lines: duḥkha dūre gela, cintā nā rahila,

blocks.text: ‘Tuya’ means ‘Your’, i.e. Supreme Lord’s lotus feet, where I have surrendered myself completely. So, if one fully surrenders to Supreme Lord, he would be at peace. All his unhappiness will go away, and there would be no more anxieties. He would see happiness in all directions.
Your lotus feet are reservoirs of immortal nectar where one may live free from sorrow and fear.
Now I have found actual peace/rest there and have given up the fear of worldly existence.

Tomara samsara … In Your (Supreme Lord’s) world. We should render service in His world (Sri Krishna’s household) and not ask for any fruits of that service. But rather we should strive for whatever pleases Him, fully devoted to His lotus feet.

lines: āmi to’ tomāra, tumi to’ āmāra,

blocks.text: I am of Supreme Lord, this body is also of Him. And He is mine. Then what need is there of any other wealth?

We have come in this world after forgetting Supreme Lord. Any moment these worldly relations can come to an end. We have been through millions of births. After passing through eight million species, human life is attained. There are four hundred thousand human species. Only in human form Supreme Lord has given intelligence to discriminate between eternal and non-eternal. One should give up non-eternal and accept eternal and worship Supreme Lord. Therefore, we should not lose this opportunity. Later whether we will get a human form is not guaranteed. The way one thinks at the time of death next life is attained.

E.g. King Bharat in his young age itself, left his wife and children and went to the forest for performing bhajan. Bhajan cannot be performed in worldly life. Once he went to fetch water from a spring. At that time there was a roar of a lion by which a pregnant she-deer got scared. She jumped across and her baby fell in water. She fell on the other side and died. Bharat Maharaja saw that child will also not survive and felt compassionate towards him. He picked up that baby and brought with him and assumed its responsibility considering his mother is not there. Ironically though Bharat Maharaja had renounced the world he went to a village to get milk for the child deer. Gradually the child grew up. The deer had very beautiful eyes. Bharat Maharaja got attached to this deer. He was always thinking of this deer, how to protect him from ferocious animals. Even at the time of death he was thinking of that deer—who will look after him after me? He left his body while thinking of that deer.
At the time of death whatever you will think, you will have birth accordingly.

So, he became a deer in his next life. However, his bhajan was not destroyed. He remembered his previous life and spent his deer-life near the hermitage of rishi-munis. In the next life he became Jada Bharat—while he was in knowledge he posed as ignorant.
So, there is no guarantee that you will achieve the next life as human being. Therefore, it’s said:

lines: tūrṇaṁ yateta na pated anu-mṛtyu yāvan

blocks.text: Our Param Gurudeva, grand Gurudeva, most venerable Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur explained this verse for a month yet he was not satisfied. This very rare human life is obtained after extreme difficulties.
Arthadam … However, in human life you can achieve the ultimate objective i.e. the complete reality. Until you achieve complete reality you will not achieve complete peace.
Complete reality is Supreme Lord. I can achieve that Supreme Lord in human life.

lines: yasmin vijñate sarvam idam vijñatam bhavati
yasmin prapte sarvam idam praptam bhavati

blocks.text: By knowing and gaining Whom, we will know and gain everything.
Upon gaining Him he thinks there is no greater gain. Being situated in such a position, one is never shaken, even in the midst of greatest difficulty.
Anityam—however this human life will not stay for long. Any moment it can go.
Tūrṇaṁ yateta—Therefore immediately, without a moment’s delay you start bhajan.

One day, as I heard from our Gurudeva, when our Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur was explaining this verse, two students of Scottish Church College of Kolkata, they are coming from the college and going to their homes. On the way they have heard that some great saint is there. Let us see. With hands filled with their books they entered and sat behind other devotees. They saw Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami Thakur, a dazzling personality, and golden complexion. They had never seen such person. They were very much attracted (and curious). He was explaining this ‘tūrṇaṁ yateta’. Don’t make late, immediately, just this moment (start Haribhajan). Don’t spoil your time, a moment’s time without serving Krishna. ‘Tūrṇaṁ yateta’, so immediately you should start, he said this looking at the two new students. They sat at the end. They were afraid, “What is this? This Swamiji is looking at us, why? Will he not allow us to go from this place?” They asked,”Swamiji, what do you want to say? You do not allow us to go to our house? Oh No! We have committed a great mistake,” (they thought) inside. Now they thought, “How we can get ourselves freed from this place? We have to go back to our house.”
They thought, Let us say this reason. “Swamiji, if my house catches fire, am I not to go there to extinguish it?”
“If your house will burn, what can you do? Nothing.”
“What sort of Sadhu! Even if my house gets burnt, you think it to be nothing?”
“Yes, nothing.”
“If I could not extinguish that fire then other houses will burn.”
“Let the whole world get burnt, what do you lose? You brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā. You are not jada bhūta i.e. you are consciousness not matter. Consciousness begets matter and not vice versa."
Nothing can’t produce something. From complete consciousness (Supreme Lord) have all the conscious entities emerged. We have not come from matter. Even the whole universe is burnt we lose nothing.
in Gita it is said. Brahma-bhūtaḥ, you are conscious entity.
Now while returning home you will not die, who can say that? Therefore, now when you have understood you should start immediately. These boys could never go home from there.

(Similarly, there was a boy who once followed Prabhupad in an ox-cart. Just by seeing him he was so attracted that he left his house. Because they are awakened souls. An awakened soul can awaken thousands and millions of people. But if all are sleeping who will wake up whom? (Guru Maharaja says jokingly…) So there is danger in going near a sadhu. But there is no danger in coming to a person like me.)
You will find sense enjoyment, sabda, rasa, rupa, gandha, sparsha in every species. However, you can worship Supreme Lord only in human life.

So you should enter worldly life by making Krishna as centre. Worldly relations are perishable. When you don’t serve Supreme Lord as master or friend or son or husband you will get worldly master or friend or husband or son. All our relationships are with Him.

(On being asked to bless the devotee so that he assimilates these teachings Gurudeva says) – He will be able to understand. Because Supreme Lord is residing inside the heart. He is closest... īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe ’rjuna tiṣṭhati.

articles.title: Recognizing the Divinity
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Rakshak Sridhar Deva Goswami Maharaja
articles.excerpt: We must have knowledge of what we are seeking. Otherwise, we will be exploited by merchants. Everywhere in every stage of life such understanding must be with us. So, it is also in the case of divinity, transcendental truth. It is also possible to develop the transcendental eye, transcendental capacity and judgement. That must be with us.

blocks.text: Student: Mahārāj, if prasādam is distributed to the mass of people, they benefit, yes?
Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj: It depends upon who is the director, who is at the bottom. It depends on him: his connection with divinity.
Student: As to whether it is properly sanctified?

Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj: The current must be there. Only wiring has no value. Do you follow? It may be connecting wiring but have no current. So, Vaikuṇṭha-Nāma-grahanam, the Vaikuṇṭha connection, the transcendental connection, must be there. Otherwise, form is form; it is useless. The spirit must be within the form. The form is also necessary; wiring is also necessary to utilise the electric current, but mere wiring has no utility. The current must be there.

So, prasādam distribution and all such things may only be an external exhibition. If real connection with divinity is present, then they are not, but otherwise, they may all be trade. An ulterior motive may be there as a business. The jāti-goswāmīs read the Bhāgavata and take money as a class of trade. If the man who is at the back has sincere connection with the Lord, then that connection comes and pervades everywhere. Then, there is prasādam. Otherwise, there is only imitation, and imitation is not the real thing.

So, Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur said that in a congregation kīrtan, a saṅkīrtan, at least one man, the leader of the party, must be śuddha-bhakta, a pure devotee. When a kīrtan party is guided under a pure devotee, then we shall join. Otherwise, we all will be dancing and jumping in the mundane plane. The connection must be there, the electric connection.
Student: How can one perceive that connection?
Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj: One who has the eye can see. We have to get the eye:
Our own realization will be the guarantee, our own knowledge. With that we will see, and that sort of eye is given by Gurudev.

The cataract is removed by Gurudev. He gives the divya-darśan, the divine eye, divya-chakṣu, that is, dīkṣā. Dīkṣā means divyaṁ jñānaṁ yato dadyāt: transcendental knowledge is imparted, and as much as one has got that sort of knowledge, one can detect the divine connection.

It is the same in other fields and other cases. How you can know whether a stone is a gem? Whether a metal is gold or brass? How can you detect whether something is glass or diamond? Who can consider this things? Expert knowledge must be there, and one who has that knowledge can detect others who have it. Fools, ordinary persons, the ignorant—they cannot differentiate.

This point is applicable everywhere. Whenever we go to purchase anything, medicine or this or that, everything may be tampered with or be an imitation. How can we understand whether this is the case? Expert knowledge must be there. Similarly, what is mundane and what is transcendental? What is sincere sevā? What is meant for the service of the Lord and what is for some ulterior purpose? One who has the fine eye can detect this.

Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur says we shall serve the Vaiṣṇavas, but before that we shall have to get the capacity to recognise who is Vaiṣṇava and who is not a Vaiṣṇava. Someone’s figure, tilak, mālā, and dress cannot be the criterion as to whether they are a sādhu.
All these things we are to understand, and that capacity of recognition is possible. That is dīkṣā, divya-jñān.

We are all expert in some stage or in some plane, and there we are to differentiate things everywhere and every time. In marketing, or in this, or in that, we are to discriminate. We must have knowledge of what we are seeking. Otherwise, we will be exploited by merchants. Everywhere in every stage of life such understanding must be with us. So, it is also in the case of divinity, transcendental truth. It is also possible to develop the transcendental eye, transcendental capacity and judgement. That must be with us.
Hare Kṛṣṇa. Gaurahari.

articles.title: Why is There a Disciplic Succession?
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Promode Puri Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: In this world, many people are contaminated by the impersonalist doctrine and thus fall into a life of sin. If there were no disciplic succession, or institution of devotees free of this contamination, then it would be very difficult for ordinary people to find saintly association. This is why the Padma Purana tells us, 'Any mantra that does not come in disciplic succession is considered to be fruitless. Therefore, four divine individuals will appear in the age of Kali to establish disciplic schools.'

blocks.text: Our worshipable predecessor, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura, wrote in Jaiva Dharma (Chapter 13). There, in response to the question, “Why is there a disciplic succession?” he writes:

'In this world, many people are contaminated by the impersonalist doctrine and thus fall into a life of sin. If there were no disciplic succession, or institution of devotees free of this contamination, then it would be very difficult for ordinary people to find saintly association. This is why the Padma Purana tells us, 'Any mantra that does not come in disciplic succession is considered to be fruitless. Therefore, four divine individuals will appear in the age of Kali to establish disciplic schools.' Of these four schools, the oldest is the Brahma sampradaya. This disciplic succession has existed since the time of Lord Brahma and is still strong. Whatever scriptures—whether Veda, Vedanta or other—are taught in a particular school maintain their original form; no interpolations are possible in these texts. Thus there can be no doubt about the mantras that are found in the books of these ancient schools. Thus a disciplic succession of saintly persons is an absolute necessity for human society and that is why the institution has existed since the earliest times.'

Bhaktivinoda Thakura continues his discussion of the subject by asking the question, 'Is the list of names of spiritual masters in the disciplic succession given without any breaks?' His answer: 'From time to time, only the more important spiritual masters' names are included in these lists.'

Every disciple has the duty to remember the names of the spiritual masters in his disciplic succession as a part of his daily meditation. This is confirmed by Baladeva Vidyabhusana in his Prameya-ratnavali (1.4):
'The learned disciple should daily remember the entire flawless disciplic succession. From them comes single-minded devotion, and from such devotion, the pleasure of Lord Hari.'

Srila Prabhupada comments: 'The disciple purifies his own character by hearing and discussing the exemplary lives of the previous spiritual masters. As his character is purified, he identifies himself as a servant of the pure devotees. He thus receives the blessings of the Lord to engage in bhajanawithout distractions. Narottama Dasaa Thakura says that Nityananda's lotus feet are eternal, and the servant of Lord Nityananda is also eternal. When the living being abandons his materialistic way of thinking and takes shelter of the transcendental lotus feet of the spiritual master, he attains the eternal spiritual world and his greatest good.' (Gaudiya-bhasya)

In the Gaudiya Vaisnava world today, there are a few short-sighted individuals who wish to disavow any connection to the Brahma-Madhva sampradaya and consider the Gaudiya disciplic succession to have come into being with Mahaprabhu himself. But we have to ask the question why Mahaprabhu accepted Madhavendra Puri into his spiritual lineage? Bhaktivinoda Thakura took up this question in his Mahaprabhura Siksa as well:

'Nimbarka Acarya's doctrine of 'difference and non-difference' (bhedabheda) was inadequate. With the advent of Lord Caitanya and his teachings, the Vaisnava world finally received this doctrine in its complete form. Madhvacarya accepted the idea of the Lord's eternal form of consciousness and bliss (sac-cid-ananda-vigraha) and because this is the basis of the acintya-bhedabheda concept, Mahaprabhu accepted the disciplic line that came from Madhva.

'Previously, the Vaisnava acaryas had some technical points of difference in their teachings and this resulted in the establishment of different religious schools. Only with the advent of the Supreme Truth himself in the form of Lord Caitanya, could the lacunae in these various doctrines be corrected as a result of his omniscience. Mahaprabhu combined Nimbarka's 'oneness in difference' with the concept of the sac-cid-ananda-vigraha of the Supreme Lord found in Madhva's teachings, Ramanuja's concept of the Lord's energy (sakti), Visnu Svami's idea of purified non-dualism (suddhadvaita) and the dedication of the Lord to His own devotees (tadiya-sarvasvata). By this most scientific doctrine, which he named acintya-bhedabheda, Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu showered his mercy on the entire universe.

'In a very short time, there will exist only one school of Vaisnava teaching, which will be named the Brahma sampradaya. All other Vaisnava schools will come into the fold of that one disciplic succession.'
